ColonyCouncil.TopicDef.label: the vote
ColonyCouncil.TopicDef.viewFor: cares a great deal how the colony votes
ColonyCouncil.TopicDef.viewAgainst: says the vote changes nothing that matters

rulesStrings.li: r_logentry->[INITIATOR_nameDef] and [RECIPIENT_nameDef] talked about the vote.
r_logentry->[INITIATOR_nameDef] asked [RECIPIENT_nameDef] who [RECIPIENT_pronoun] meant to vote for.
r_logentry->[INITIATOR_nameDef] and [RECIPIENT_nameDef] went over the candidates for the council.
r_logentry->[INITIATOR_nameDef] told [RECIPIENT_nameDef] how [INITIATOR_pronoun] thought the vote would go.

plain.li: [for] Have you made up your mind about the vote for {SUBJECT}?
[for] This vote matters more than people think.
[for,lean:holder] I'm keeping the same {SUBJECT}, the work's been done well enough.
[for,lean:other] I think it's time we had a new {SUBJECT}.
[for,lean:self] I'm standing for {SUBJECT}, and I'd like your vote.
[for,undecided] I still don't know who I'll vote for as {SUBJECT}.
[for,standing] I've been asking everyone what they want from the next {SUBJECT}.
[for,holder] I'd like another year as {SUBJECT}, if the colony will have me.
[against] Whoever wins, the same work gets done by the same people.
[against] It's a vote for a chair, nothing more.
[against,lean:holder] I'll vote to keep things as they are and stop thinking about it.
[against,lean:other] I'll vote for a change, not that it'll make much difference.
[against,undecided] I haven't thought about the vote, and I'm not going to.
[mixed] I go back and forth on the vote for {SUBJECT}.
[mixed,undecided] Both of them would do, which makes it harder to choose.
[mixed,lean:other] I'm leaning toward someone new, but I could be talked out of it.

warm.li: [for] Whoever wins, I hope they're kind about it.
[for,lean:holder] I think the one we have deserves another year.

blunt.li: [against] The vote's a waste of an evening.

cheerful.li: [for] I love a vote, everyone's so polite to each other for a week.

gloomy.li: [against] Whoever we pick, we'll be complaining about them by winter.

cold.li: [for] The vote decides who decides, so it's worth getting right.

plain.li: [agree,for] It matters, and I'm glad someone else thinks so.
[agree,lean:holder] I'm keeping the one we have too.
[agree,lean:other] I'm voting for a change as well.
[agree,undecided] I haven't decided either, so we can be undecided together.
[agree,lean:self] I'm standing too, so we'll see which of us they choose.
[agree,against] It won't change much, I agree.
[agree] That's more or less where I am.
[debate,lean:holder] The one we have has done well enough to keep.
[debate,lean:other] A new face would do the seat some good.
[debate,undecided] I'll listen to the speeches before I choose.
[debate,for] It's worth thinking about properly, at least.
[debate,against] It's one vote among many, I won't lose sleep over it.
[argue,lean:holder] You'd throw out someone who's done the work for nothing.
[argue,lean:other] Another year of the same, that's what you want?
[argue,against] If you don't care, don't vote.
[argue,for] It's not a game, people's lives depend on who sits there.

warm.li: [agree] I'm glad we see it the same way.

plain.li: [agree] We'll see how it goes at the count, then.
[agree,lean:self] Thank you, I'll try to deserve it.
[agree,for] I'll see you at the vote.
[debate] Vote how you like, and I'll do the same.
[debate,undecided] Tell me if you make up your mind.
[debate,for] We'll find out soon enough who was right.
[argue] We'll have to vote against each other, then.
[argue,against] Fine, stay home on the day.
[agree,against] Either way, the fields still need doing.

warm.li: [debate] Whoever wins, we'll still have supper together.

plain.li: [debate] Maybe, we'll see.
[debate,undecided] I'll decide on the day.
[debate,lean:other] I still think it's time for someone new.
[debate,lean:holder] I still think we should keep who we have.
[argue] My vote's my own business.
[argue,lean:self] I'll win without yours, then.
